'''Eleanor Philbrook Cushing''' (December 27, 1856 – April 21, 1925) was an American mathematics professor, on the faculty of [[Smith College]] from 1881 to 1922.

== Early life and education ==
Cushing was born in [[Bath, Maine]], the daughter of Samuel Woodward Cushing and Mary Ann Mereen Cushing. Her father was a merchant. Her brother William Lee Cushing taught Latin at Yale and ran the [[Westminster School (Connecticut)|Westminster School]] in Connecticut. Playwright [[Tom Cushing]] was her nephew.<ref>{{Cite book|last=University|first=Yale|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A55GAQAAMAAJ&dq=Samuel+Woodward+Cushing&pg=PA362|title=Obiturary Record of Graduates|date=1921|publisher=Tuttle, Morehouse & Taylor Company|pages=362–364|language=en}}</ref> 

Cushing was a member of Smith College's first graduating class in 1879.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|date=July 1922|title=Eleanor Philbrook Cushing|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sMPOAAAAMAAJ&dq=Eleanor+P.+Cushing&pg=RA1-PA345|journal=The Smith Alumnae Quarterly|volume=13|pages=345–349}}</ref> She earned a master's degree in 1882.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Leonard|first=John W.|date=1914|title=Woman's who's who of America: a biographical dictionary of contemporary women of the United States and Canada.|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/001717980|pages=224}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating from Smith College, she taught school in Bath and [[New Haven, Connecticut|New Haven]], then became a member of the Smith College faculty from 1881<ref>{{Cite book|last=Seelye|first=Laurenus Clark|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IeFlPeUy2hcC&dq=Eleanor+P.+Cushing&pg=PA54|title=The Early History of Smith College, 1871-1910|date=1923|publisher=Houghton Mifflin|pages=54|language=en}}</ref> to 1922, as professor of mathematics and chair of the department.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Green|first1=Judy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&dq=Eleanor+Cushing+math&pg=PA27|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|date=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5|pages=27|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Smith College|url=http://archive.org/details/class1907smit|title=Class of 1907 Classbook|date=1907|publisher=Smith College|others=College Archives Smith College Libraries|pages=16}}</ref> She was also president of the college's Alumnae Association and the undergraduate Mathematics Club.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 1920|title=Club Activities|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gdZNAQAAMAAJ&dq=Eleanor+Cushing+math&pg=PA184|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|volume=27|pages=184}}</ref> 

In 1890, she was named to the Commission Of Colleges On Admission Examinations In New England.<ref>{{Cite book|last=England|first=Commission Of Colleges On Admission Examinations In New|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YNUrAAAAYAAJ&dq=Eleanor+P.+Cushing&pg=RA3-PA6|title=Annual Report|date=1890|pages=6|language=en}}</ref> "It displeased her to be called professor and she could not be persuaded to wear an academic cap and gown—never appearing where they were required," [[Laurenus Clark Seelye]] recalled of Cushing's disdain for "ostentatious display". She resigned as professor emerita, and retired to Maine.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Cushing inherited a [[Queen Anne style architecture|Queen Anne-style]] house in [[Northampton, Massachusetts]] from her friend, Elizabeth Jarvis Hopkins. She lived there from 1897 to 1922, then donated the building to Smith College.<ref>[http://www.historic-northampton.org/members_only/histimages/FormB/hnformb707.pdf E. Hopkins House], Massachusetts Historical Commission.</ref> She died in 1925, in Bath, aged 69 years.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1925-04-22|title=Early Smith Graduate|pages=3|work=The Portsmouth Herald|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/86771545/early-smith-graduate/|access-date=2021-10-09|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YmY0AQAAMAAJ&dq=Eleanor+Philbrook+Cushing+Died+Maine&pg=PA179|title=Annual Report|date=1925|publisher=The Foundation|pages=179–180|language=en}}</ref> Cushing House residence which was built in 1922 on the campus of Smith College is named for her.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cushing House|url=https://www.smith.edu/student-life/residence-life/houses/cushing-house|access-date=2021-10-09|website=Smith College|language=en}}</ref>
